possibleCauses: Blocked drain filter or lint trap
Drain pipe set higher than the machine allows
tips: Run the machine on empty after clearing the filter to see if it drains.
Keep the drain hose free of sharp bends.

possibleCauses: Load unbalanced on one side of the drum
Faulty door lock stopping the spin cycle
tips: Redistribute the load evenly and try a spin-only cycle.

possibleCauses: Cracked outer tub or damaged pump seal
tips: Turn the inlet tap off until the visit to limit water damage.

possibleCauses: Transit bolts still fitted after a move
Machine not levelled on the floor
A coin or clip caught between drum and tub
tips: Check the machine does not rock when pushed at a corner.

possibleCauses: No power at the socket or a tripped MCB
Control board or power supply fault
tips: Try another appliance on the same socket to rule out the supply.

possibleCauses: Water inlet or drain fault reported by a sensor
Temperature or level sensor out of range
tips: Note the exact code — it narrows the fault considerably.

possibleCauses: Water still standing in the drum
Power interrupted before the cycle ended
tips: Switch off at the wall for a minute, then power back on.

possibleCauses: Low refrigerant from a slow leak
Dirty condenser coil on the outdoor unit
tips: Rinse the filters and let them dry fully before refitting.

possibleCauses: Blocked drain line or drain pan
Frozen coil melting faster than it drains
tips: Switch the unit off to stop the drip until the visit.

possibleCauses: Mould in the blower wheel or coil
Standing water in the drain pan
Dust burning off the heating element
Dead insect or debris inside the unit
tips: A deep clean usually clears this where a normal service will not.
Note whether the noise is from the indoor or the outdoor unit.

possibleCauses: Remote batteries dead or remote unpaired
Faulty PCB on the indoor unit
Failed capacitor on the outdoor unit
tips: Try the manual power button on the indoor unit.

possibleCauses: Restricted airflow from a dirty filter
tips: Run the fan without cooling for an hour to let the ice melt.

possibleCauses: Short in the compressor or fan winding
tips: Leave the MCB off until an expert has looked at it.

possibleCauses: Thermostat set too low or faulty
Dust-clogged condenser coil at the back
tips: Leave a 10cm gap behind the fridge for airflow.

possibleCauses: Door seal letting warm air in
tips: Manual defrosting helps briefly but the cause will return.

possibleCauses: Water line or filter leak on a dispenser model
tips: Dry the floor under it so you can tell if the leak is ongoing.

possibleCauses: Fridge not level on the floor
Ice touching the evaporator fan blade
tips: Note when the noise happens — constant or only in cycles.

possibleCauses: Door hinge dropped out of alignment
Shelf or drawer fouling the door
tips: A note of paper should grip when closed in the door.

possibleCauses: Poor door seal letting warm air in
tips: Check nothing is holding a door slightly open.

possibleCauses: Blown bulb or failed LED strip
tips: If cooling is normal, this is usually a small part swap.
Check the indicator lamp — no lamp usually means no supply.

possibleCauses: Heavy scale on the heating element
Tank capacity too small for the demand
tips: Hard water areas need descaling roughly once a year.
Turn the geyser off at the MCB and shut the inlet valve.
Do not reset repeatedly — a tripping geyser is a shock risk.
Compare the cold tap pressure at the same outlet.

possibleCauses: Scale on the element boiling unevenly
tips: A flush and descale clears most rumbling.
If the turntable and light still work, it is usually the magnetron side.
Stop using it until it is checked — sparking can start a fire.

possibleCauses: Control board not driving the motor
tips: Lift the plate out and refit it on the coupler.
Look for a lock icon on the display before booking.
A door that will not latch stops the microwave from running at all.
Note whether the noise only starts when it is heating.
